vsm1.9:6.5: 1. “‘Fighting against the wall’: having undertaken the precepts of virtue and sat down on a seat in his room with the door locked, he was developing loving-kindness. Blinded by lust arisen under cover of the loving-kindness, he wanted to go to his wife, and without noticing the door he beat on the wall in his desire to get out even by breaking the wall down” (Vism-mhṭ 286).
vsm1.9:11.1: 2. Reading dāna-piyavacanādīni with Ce (see four saṅgahavatthūni—A II 32).
vsm1.9:15.5: 3. The Aṅguttara text has “Let him … reappear in a state of loss” and so on.
vsm1.9:20.1: 4. “The eight great hells beginning with that of Sañjīva (see J-a V 266, 270). At each of the four doors of the Great Unmitigated (Avīci) Hell there are the four beginning with the Ember (Kukuḷa) Hell (M III 185), which make up the sixteen prominent hells” (Vism-mhṭ 291).
